chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Sabih, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The blood-money of a hunting dog (Saluqi) is forty dirhams, as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered for the tribe of Khuza'ah.

key_terms.السَّلُوقِيُّ: A specific breed of swift hunting dog

ai.seo_question: What is the blood-money value for a hunting dog in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the specific blood-money (diyah) for a hunting dog as forty dirhams, explicitly linking this ruling to a directive from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) applied to the tribe of Khuza'ah. It illustrates the continuity of legal authority from the Prophet to the Imams, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet's direct instructions being preserved and transmitted through reliable chains to define practical jurisprudence regarding property and compensation.
